request.description: Measure the compiled two-joint arm's candidate-independent inertial, actuator, singular-start, and reversal response envelope under the production 2 ms physics and 10-substep held-action timing.
request.rationale: The initial decision is whether the first capability effort should primarily correct the training distribution or address a physical/control transient bottleneck. The measurement uses the human-authored XML and records compiled inertias, damping, armature, actuator transmission, configuration-dependent mass matrices, and full 2 ms traces from reset-like, open-bent, and folded-bent starts under a bounded action followed by its sign reversal. If reset-like radial authority is transiently poor but bent-state response and reversal settle quickly, official-range exposure and trajectory-aware learning are the credible first direction; if response is slow or reversal leaves large residual motion across bent states, low-level action shaping/control bandwidth becomes the priority; if compiled contacts or constraints appear, the free-space model must be revised before attributing failures to learning.

request.description: Train the existing PPO MlpPolicy recipe from scratch with the training target radius changed from the outer band to the complete official 0.06-0.20 m interval.
request.rationale: M2 measured strong direct-actuation authority but a singular reset departure and high transient kinetic energy; it did not establish learned performance. The repository's clearest known confound is the prior 0.14-0.20 m training exposure versus the official 0.06-0.20 m distribution. This run tests whether full-radius exposure improves the complete reach-and-hold capability without changing observations, reward, physics, action timing, policy architecture, or evaluation semantics.

request.description: Evaluate T1:checkpoint-120832 on the held-out 160-episode research panel with per-episode geometry and reach/hold diagnostics.
request.rationale: Training proxies nominate T1:checkpoint-120832 as the current candidate, but only research evaluation establishes development behavior. The artifact's target-radius, first-reach, minimum/final distance, maximum held steps, in-tolerance steps, and hold-interruption fields will test whether full-radius exposure closes the inner-band gap and whether failures are primarily trajectory/convergence or post-entry stabilization. This is a development measurement distinct from the protected 200-episode official assessment.

request.description: Re-evaluate T1:checkpoint-120832 on the same 160-episode panel to preserve failure trajectories with post-step q/qdot, end-effector velocity, Jacobian determinant, and contact count.
request.rationale: M3 established 93.75% development success but its compact diagnostics cannot distinguish the observed angular no-entry failures from joint-limit/branch or dynamic trajectory causes. The evaluator now adds failure-only outer-step traces while preserving the exact task outcome and panel. Reusing the same candidate and seeds makes the outcome comparison direct; the new trace fields are the discriminating evidence, not a replacement success criterion.

request.reason: This is the strongest completed candidate evidence: it was trained on the complete official radial interval with the existing PPO feed-forward method and achieved 150/160 (93.75%) on the held-out research panel. M4 preserved the same outcome and adds failure traces showing zero contacts, several shoulder-limit-adjacent no-entry trajectories, and two high-interruption hold failures. It is below the human goal, but stronger than any other candidate because no alternative candidate has completed development evaluation.

request.candidates_and_roles: Best-known: T1:checkpoint-120832, explicitly assigned by E1 on the basis of M3/M4. No working candidate is assigned. No retained candidates. The candidate is below the human goal and has not been officially assessed.
request.cumulative_resource_use: Completed one candidate-independent dynamics measurement (M2), one fresh 120000-step training allocation (T1; actual terminal checkpoint 120832 due rollout rounding), two 160-episode development measurements on the same candidate and panel (M3 and M4), and one best-known role assignment (E1). No protected official assessment has been requested or consumed.
request.current_goal_gap: The best-known candidate T1:checkpoint-120832 achieved 150/160 = 93.75% on the held-out development panel, leaving 10 development failures and a 4.25 percentage-point shortfall to 98% on that panel. This is development evidence, not an official assessment; the protected 200-episode result remains unmeasured.
request.current_synthesis: Observed facts: M2 compiled the human-authored model as a two-DOF, two-actuator system with 2 ms physics, 10-step held controls, zero gravity, 0.5 joint damping, 0.01 armature, gear 5, and configuration-dependent mass matrices near 0.01 kg*m^2. In the fixed bounded diagnostic, reset begins with a near-zero planar Jacobian determinant (about 1e-5), while a held [0.5,-0.5] command rapidly creates joint speed and kinetic energy; after sign reversal the arm still has substantial residual speed at the end of the 0.4 s phase. This supports a singular-departure and braking/settling concern, but the diagnostic is not a learned-policy evaluation and does not establish a torque unit beyond the compiled control interface. T1 changed only training radius exposure to the complete official 0.06-0.20 m interval; its learning proxies rose to 0.58 at the terminal saved checkpoint but do not establish performance. M3 measured that checkpoint at 93.75% (150/160); M4 repeated the same panel and outcome while adding failure traces. In M3/M4, eight of ten failures never entered the tolerance disk, two entered but had maximum held runs of only 1 and 3 with many interruptions. Failures were not confined to the newly exposed inner radii and included a negative-angle cluster. M4 traces show zero contacts in inspected failed episodes and several trajectories ending with shoulder qpos near +/-2.975 rad, adjacent to the +/-170 degree joint limit, while other failures retain large residual joint speed. Interpretation: unreachable-target and contact explanations are weakened; the evidence instead supports competing angular branch/joint-limit trajectory failure and high-energy braking/convergence failure. Full-radius exposure is a promising candidate property but not a causal conclusion because no matched outer-band candidate was evaluated. The current evidence does not yet establish whether explicit branch feasibility/limit awareness, action saturation/braking, or another policy difference removes the failures.
request.decision_frontier: The unresolved decision is whether the remaining gap is best attacked as an angular IK-branch/joint-limit trajectory problem or as a general high-velocity braking and stabilization problem. Discriminating evidence should preserve target radius/angle, both analytic IK candidates and their joint-limit margins, policy q/qdot/action traces, Jacobian determinant, first reach, and hold interruptions for failed and matched successful targets. A failure field concentrated at infeasible or low-margin branches and shoulder-limit excursions would justify branch/limit-aware trajectory design; failures with feasible high-margin branches but large qdot and repeated disk exits would justify braking/action-smoothing or stabilization work. Current M4 has q/qdot/J/action/contact traces but not analytic candidate margins, so it narrows rather than closes this distinction.
request.human_goal_connection: Advance toward a learned policy with at least 98% success on the protected official 200-episode task by first separating physical feasibility, transient control, and learning-exposure effects, then targeting the failure mechanism that can remove the remaining development failures without changing the task boundary.
request.next_direction_or_closure: End startup with this checkpoint and enter goal review. Prefer opening the proposed bounded inquiry because the best-known candidate is materially below the goal, its failures are mechanism-structured rather than purely inner-radius, and M4 supplies enough evidence to design a discriminating branch/limit-versus-braking test. Do not request official assessment yet.
request.next_question: In a bounded inquiry, can a branch- and joint-limit-aware trajectory/stabilization method remove the observed angular no-entry and high-interruption failures while preserving the complete official radial distribution and sampled uninterrupted-hold semantics?

request.closure_condition: Close when matched full-radius evidence has classified the residual failures using target geometry, both analytic IK candidates and their joint-limit margins, q/qdot/action/Jacobian and first-reach traces, and hold interruptions, and either (a) a mechanism-targeted candidate comparison shows a complete-artifact improvement in uninterrupted-hold success and the corresponding failure class, (b) the evidence redirects the campaign to the competing mechanism, or (c) the test is inconclusive and preserves the unresolved distinction for goal review. Aggregate reward or a new method description alone is insufficient.
request.goal_connection: The best-known policy reaches only 150/160 successes (93.75%) on the development panel, below the 98% campaign objective. Removing the remaining failures requires distinguishing the observed no-entry/limit excursions from residual-velocity and interrupted-hold failures before spending another bounded training allocation, while preserving the official 0.06-0.20 m radial distribution, full angular range, 1 cm tolerance, 100 consecutive post-block checks, and 200-episode assessment boundary.

The inquiry instead requires a discriminating mechanism test followed by a complete candidate comparison; claims will remain limited to the implemented variant and its matched evidence.

request.description: Fresh PPO training with the official full 0.06-0.20 m radius exposure and the original runtime/reward, using a 15-value observation that appends signed open/folded IK candidate joint-limit margins to expose branch feasibility.
request.rationale: M5 showed the dominant structured failure: seven of ten failures approached the open branch despite that branch being infeasible or reaching a negative actual shoulder-limit margin, while a folded feasible branch existed in six cases. This run tests that supported mechanism alone by changing only the observation to make candidate limit feasibility explicit; it does not add braking, velocity, reward, action, target, or hold changes. A subsequent matched development evaluation will compare complete artifacts against T1 and inspect whether no-entry/limit failures decline without claiming that residual-velocity failures are solved.

request.description: Evaluate T2:checkpoint-120832, the branch-feasibility-aware fresh candidate selected from T2 learning dynamics, on the same 160-episode full-radius development panel at seed 4200 with schema-7 mechanism diagnostics.
request.rationale: This is the complete-artifact test of the mechanism-targeted observation variant. T2 changed the policy input by appending signed open/folded IK joint-limit margins while preserving the PPO recipe, action mapping, target exposure, physics, and sampled hold semantics; saved-component comparisons show it is not an exact serialized match to T1. Compare its uninterrupted success and failure fields to M5/T1:checkpoint-120832. Improvement concentrated in the prior infeasible-open/limit failure class would support the branch mechanism; unchanged or worse performance, especially with the high-margin velocity failures persisting, limits the tested intervention and redirects the next decision rather than establishing that branch information is ineffective in general.

request.outcome: Limited and inconclusive intervention result. M5 resolved the dominant T1 failure pattern on the matched full-radius panel: 7/10 failures were no-entry or interrupted approaches to the open IK branch despite an infeasible or negative-margin shoulder configuration, while 2/10 entered feasible high-margin configurations with large residual velocity and repeated interruptions; one no-entry case had both branches high-margin. The branch-feasibility observation variant T2 did not improve the complete artifact: its selected checkpoint achieved 25/160 = 15.625% versus T1/M5 at 150/160 = 93.75%, with zero training success across T2 checkpoints and 113/160 no-entry episodes. This negative result is a property of the tested fresh PPO implementation, not evidence that branch-aware control is intrinsically ineffective. The branch-versus-stabilization distinction is therefore classified for T1 but the effective remedy remains unresolved; T1 remains best-known and the protected 200-episode objective is unmet.
request.reason: The inquiry closure condition is met by matched mechanism evidence plus a complete-artifact comparison that is negative but scientifically non-diagnostic about the intended branch feature because T2 training collapsed. The result redirects the next decision away from another unvalidated observation-only run: goal review should decide whether to develop an explicitly branch-selecting/trajectory-aware controller while separately controlling residual velocity, or request assessment of T1. Preserve the competing high-margin stabilization failure and the limitation that no braking intervention was tested.

T2:checkpoint-120832 is an experimental branch-feasibility observation variant with 15.625% development success in M6 and is not best-known. No working or retained candidate. T2's complete artifact is not scientifically adequate for selection, and the terminal checkpoint is not privileged by position.
request.cumulative_resource_use: Campaign to date: M2 candidate-independent dynamics measurement; T1 fresh 120000-step baseline training with full-radius exposure; M3 and M4 matched 160-episode T1 development measurements; E1 best-known assignment; E2 goal-review checkpoint; E3 inquiry opening; E4 inquiry-session checkpoint; M5 matched schema-7 mechanism rerun; T2 fresh 120000-step branch-feasibility observation training; M6 matched 160-episode T2 development measurement; E5 inquiry closure. Total: 2 fresh 120000-step training allocations (240000 requested, 241664 actual after rollout rounding), 5 completed measurements in the campaign record relevant here (M2, M3, M4, M5, M6), 2 candidate artifacts selected for development measurement (T1 and T2), 1 active inquiry opened and closed, and no protected official assessment consumed.
request.current_goal_gap: T1:checkpoint-120832 remains the strongest evidence-backed candidate at 150/160 = 93.75% on the development panel; the 4.25 percentage-point development shortfall remains, and the protected official 200-episode result is still unmeasured. The branch-aware T2 candidate achieved only 25/160 = 15.625% and is not a replacement.
request.current_synthesis: Observed facts: M5 reran T1 on the identical 160-episode full-radius panel and reproduced 150/160 success with schema-7 diagnostics. Of ten failures, seven never entered the disk; six of those approached the open analytic IK branch although its shoulder candidate was infeasible, and their actual trajectories reached negative shoulder-limit margins while a folded feasible branch existed. The seventh no-entry failure had both endpoint branches high-margin. The remaining three failures entered: one followed an infeasible open branch and reached a negative limit margin, while two had feasible high-margin branches but entered with large residual joint velocity and repeated hold interruptions (up to 192/242). All inspected traces had zero contacts. Interpretation: for the T1 artifact, branch/limit trajectory selection is the dominant structured failure class (7/10), while high-velocity braking/hold stabilization is a consequential secondary class (2/10 plus the mixed case); this supports the physical model's coupling of IK branch, joint limits, and transient energy, and weakens contact and unreachable-target explanations. T2 implemented only four signed IK-candidate limit margins as additional policy inputs; its saved components and runtime were unequal to T1, so it was a real artifact change. However, its learning dynamics reported zero training success at every checkpoint and its selected checkpoint achieved only 25/160 with 113/160 no-entry episodes. Therefore M6 establishes a negative result for this fresh PPO observation-only implementation, not that branch-aware control is ineffective in general. The branch classification is stronger than the intervention claim; the high-margin velocity mechanism remains untested as an intervention. Official sampled hold semantics and the human task boundary were unchanged throughout.
request.decision_frontier: At goal review, compare T1's 93.75% development prospect and one protected 200-episode assessment against the cost of another bounded inquiry. If continuing, the consequential unresolved method question is how to produce a viable learned trajectory that selects a feasible IK branch and brakes into a stable hold without bundling untested mechanisms or changing official semantics. Any next candidate comparison must preserve the full 0.06-0.20 m radius and angular distribution, 1 cm tolerance, 100 consecutive sampled post-block checks, and 200-episode assessment boundary; it must distinguish branch/limit failure from feasible high-margin velocity/hold failure. T2's collapse means a new branch intervention needs an explicitly viable learning signal or controller design before efficacy can be inferred.
request.human_goal_connection: Advance toward a learned policy achieving at least 98% success on the protected 200-episode official task by preserving the strongest complete artifact, resolving consequential failure mechanisms without changing the human task boundary, and deciding whether further bounded work has higher expected value than terminal assessment.
request.next_direction_or_closure: Inquiry I1 is closed with a limited/inconclusive intervention result. The mechanism evidence supports branch/limit trajectory failures as the dominant T1 gap but does not validate the observation-only remedy because T2 training collapsed; high-velocity stabilization remains a competing untested intervention. Return to goal review to choose between protected assessment of the existing best-known T1 artifact and a new bounded, explicitly viable trajectory/braking investigation. Do not claim the human goal is met.
request.next_question: Should the campaign request the protected official assessment for T1:checkpoint-120832, or open one further task-preserving inquiry to develop and compare a viable branch/trajectory controller with explicit braking diagnostics against T1?

request.reason: Request the protected official 200-episode assessment for the explicit best-known artifact T1:checkpoint-120832. T1 is the only complete policy with strong development evidence: it was trained with the full official 0.06-0.20 m radial exposure and achieved 150/160 = 93.75% on the held-out full-radius panel, reproduced on the identical panel with schema-7 diagnostics (M3, M4, M5), while preserving the official target distribution, 1 cm tolerance, 100 consecutive post-block hold checks, and unchanged physics and action timing. The physical model is supported in the tested regime: official targets have a feasible IK branch, failures showed no contacts, and the residual failures were structured mainly as branch/limit trajectory failures (7/10) with a consequential high-residual-velocity/hold-interruption class (2/10 plus one mixed case). T2 does not provide a viable replacement or a basis for another inquiry: its signed-margin observation-only implementation had zero training success at every checkpoint and only 25/160 = 15.625% development success, with unequal saved components/runtime, so this is a negative result for that fresh PPO artifact, not evidence against branch-aware control generally. No braking intervention has been tested, and the causal remedy remains unresolved; those are preserved limitations rather than reasons to treat an untested variant as a better candidate. The development score is below 98%, but the contract does not make that a barrier to assessment, and the protected 200-episode result is the direct campaign-level decision needed now. Further bounded work has no demonstrated viable complete artifact and would spend resources on an unvalidated intervention, whereas assessment of T1 directly determines whether the human goal is met or the campaign ends in failure.
